specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit unitary U to error eps by a probabilistic protocol (PQF): a finite-step walk on a Markov chain of single-qubit unitaries over a universal gate set (Clifford+T primarily), in which each step applies a multi-qubit exact unitary W_k on data+ancilla, measures the ancilla, and moves to a next unitary determined by the outcome. U_eps is absorbing and the walk terminates after finitely many steps.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful instance: 1 data qubit + 1 ancilla (2 qubits, under the 3-qubit cap), Clifford+T. A single PQF step with ancilla measured mid-circuit and classically controlled fallback correction, plus the final check that each measurement record yields a known data-qubit unitary and the expected T count is a probability-weighted sum. Outside scope: general norm-equation/factoring synthesis, the Clifford+V and Clifford+pi/12 constructions, the proof of the log_b(1/eps)+O(log log(1/eps)) bound, and explicit chain design for arbitrary U. The specific W_k, byproduct maps, and chain are not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Step transition
equations.description: Ancilla-assisted step; each outcome m implements a data-qubit unitary A_{k,m} with probability p_{k,m}. Requires each block be proportional to a unitary (assumed, to make the chain deterministic per outcome).
equations.abstract_quote: transitions are induced by multi-qubit unitaries followed by measurements
equations.justification: Abstract says transitions come from multi-qubit unitaries followed by measurements; the block form is the standard consequence; the unitary-block requirement is an assumption.
assumptions: Each outcome block is proportional to a unitary

equations.label: Markov chain next state
equations.latex: V_{k,m}=C_{k,m}\,A_{k,m}\,V_k\ \ (\text{up to global phase and Cliffords}),\quad \Pr[V_k\to V_{k,m}]=p_{k,m}
equations.description: Deterministic next state per outcome, random across outcomes; the walk on this chain is the protocol.
equations.abstract_quote: implements a walk on a discrete Markov chain in which the target unitary is an absorbing state
equations.justification: Inferred from the Markov-chain-walk description; the explicit form of the update is an assumed construction.
assumptions: Composition order and correction structure assumed

equations.label: Absorbing target
equations.description: The target state is absorbing; reaching it ends the protocol with the data qubit holding U_eps up to global phase.
equations.abstract_quote: the target unitary is an absorbing state
equations.justification: Direct reading of the absorbing-state claim; the error norm is an assumed measure.
assumptions: Distance measured up to global phase

equations.label: Expected cost
equations.description: Expected gate count as a probability-weighted sum over the finite path DAG, computed from the branching probabilities.
equations.justification: Standard expectation over a finite absorbing Markov chain; abstract mentions expected gate counts.
assumptions: Finite DAG so the sum is finite

equations.label: Claimed scaling
equations.description: Asymptotic expected gate count to be checked only qualitatively; not verifiable on tiny instances.

registers.name: anc
registers.role: ancilla measured mid-circuit; outcome selects the next W and correction

specification.initial_state: data in arbitrary |psi> (verify on basis states or via process fidelity), ancilla |0>

steps.description: Classically choose a finite chain (DAG) of states V_k, exact gate-set unitaries W_k, and corrections C_{k,m}; this synthesis is assumed given for the small instance.
At the current state k, apply W_k to data+ancilla, measure the ancilla into a classical bit, and apply the classically controlled correction C_{k,m}.
Repeat with the next state's W until reaching an absorbing state U_eps, which takes finitely many steps.
Compute the expected T count from the branch probabilities and check the data-qubit unitary per record against U_eps up to global phase.

specification.measurement: Ancilla measured mid-circuit each step (bit 0 in Qiskit little-endian ordering for that step's clbit); the data qubit is not measured, and is checked by simulation.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Feedforward selects the next W_k and correction from the outcome record; expected T count computed from the path probabilities.
assumptions: Chosen instance: 1 data + 1 ancilla, Clifford+T, a one- or two-step chain
Gate-set entries lie in a ring where norm equations are classically solvable
Mid-circuit measurement and feedforward are available
Byproduct unitaries stay in the ring so the chain is closed
Success probability is bounded below and fallback states have strictly lower cost, ensuring termination
The sketch's details (W_k, corrections, b=2 for T) are not in the abstract
